question:
Which of the following is NOT a component of the Green Revolution?

[SSC GD 2022]
options: Application of fertilisers and chemicals
Minimum support price
High yielding variety seeds
Multiple cropping pattern
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Minimum support price

Explanation:
The Green Revolution primarily aimed at increasing agricultural production through the application of fertilisers and chemicals, high-yielding variety (HYV) seeds, and multiple cropping patterns. These components were essential for boosting productivity. However, 'Minimum Support Price (MSP)' is a government policy designed to ensure farmers receive a minimum price for their crops, rather than directly increasing production. Hence, it is not a component of the Green Revolution.

Extra Facts:
The Green Revolution began in India in the 1960s, led by Dr. M.S. Swaminathan. Its main focus was on increasing the productivity of wheat and rice. This revolution made India self-sufficient in food grain production but also had negative effects, such as soil fertility depletion and water scarcity.

question_hi:
निम्नलिखित में से कौन सा हरित क्रांति का घटक नहीं है?

[SSC GD 2022]
options_hi: उर्वरकों और रसायनों के आवेदन
न्यूनतम समर्थन मूल्य
उच्च उपज देने वाली किस्म के बीज
बहुफसली प्रतिरूप
solution_hi:
हल: सही उत्तर है न्यूनतम समर्थन मूल्य

Explanation:
हरित क्रांति का मुख्य उद्देश्य कृषि उत्पादन में वृद्धि करना था, जिसमें उर्वरकों और रसायनों का उपयोग, उच्च उपज देने वाली किस्म (HYV) के बीज, और बहुफसली प्रतिरूप शामिल थे। ये सभी घटक कृषि उत्पादकता बढ़ाने के लिए आवश्यक थे। हालांकि, 'न्यूनतम समर्थन मूल्य (MSP)' एक सरकारी नीति है जिसका उद्देश्य किसानों को उनकी फसलों के लिए न्यूनतम मूल्य सुनिश्चित करना है, न कि सीधे तौर पर उत्पादन बढ़ाना। इसलिए, यह हरित क्रांति का घटक नहीं है।

Extra Facts:
हरित क्रांति 1960 के दशक में भारत में शुरू हुई, जिसका प्रमुख नेतृत्व डॉ. एम.एस. स्वामीनाथन ने किया। इसका मुख्य फोकस गेहूं और चावल की उत्पादकता बढ़ाना था। इस क्रांति ने भारत को खाद्यान्न उत्पादन में आत्मनिर्भर बनाया, लेकिन इसके कुछ नकारात्मक प्रभाव भी थे, जैसे मिट्टी की उर्वरता में कमी और जल संकट।

question:
The green revolution technology resulted in an increase in production of cereal production from 72.4 million tons in 1965-66 to _______million tons in 1978-79.

[SSC CGL 2024]
options: 150.8
165.9
131.9
141.2
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is 131.9

Explanation:
The Green Revolution in India, initiated in the 1960s, was an agricultural revolution aimed at increasing food grain production through the use of High Yielding Variety (HYV) seeds, chemical fertilizers, irrigation facilities, and modern farming techniques. As a result, cereal production rose from 72.4 million tons in 1965-66 to 131.9 million tons in 1978-79. This growth was primarily seen in wheat and rice crops, making India self-sufficient in food grains.

Extra Facts:
The key scientist behind the Green Revolution, Dr. M.S. Swaminathan, is regarded as its father. This revolution significantly boosted agricultural output in states like Punjab, Haryana, and Western Uttar Pradesh. However, it also had negative effects, such as soil fertility depletion, declining groundwater levels, and excessive use of chemical fertilizers.

question:
______ leaves are used to make bidis.

[SSC CGL 2024]
options: Neem
Champa
Betel
Tendu
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Tendu

Explanation:
Tendu leaves are primarily used for making bidis. These leaves are found abundantly in central India, particularly in Madhya Pradesh, Chhattisgarh, and Odisha. Tendu leaves are strong, flexible, and aromatic, making them ideal for rolling and maintaining the quality of bidis. It is a significant forest product that also supports the local economy.

Extra Facts:
The scientific name of the Tendu tree is Diospyros melanoxylon. It is a hardwood tree commonly found in dry deciduous forests. Apart from bidi-making, its leaves are also used in traditional medicine. The bidi industry in India provides employment to millions, with tendu leaf collection being a major activity.

question:
Which of the following is NOT a Kharif crop ?

[SSC CGL 2024]
options: Paddy
Soybean
Wheat
Cotton
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Wheat

Explanation:
Kharif crops are those crops that are sown during the monsoon season (June-July) and harvested in October-November. These crops require substantial water. Paddy, Soybean, and Cotton are major Kharif crops. Wheat, on the other hand, is a Rabi crop, sown in October-November and harvested in March-April. It grows in cooler climates and requires less water. Hence, Wheat is not a Kharif crop.

Extra Facts:
In India, crops are broadly classified into three seasons: Kharif, Rabi, and Zaid. Kharif crops also include maize, millet, groundnut, and pigeon pea. Rabi crops consist of mustard, chickpea, and barley. Zaid crops are summer-season crops like watermelon, cucumber, and muskmelon. These crops play a vital role in India's agricultural economy.

सोयाबीन

solution_hi:

Explanation:
खरीफ की फसलें वे फसलें होती हैं जो मानसून के मौसम में उगाई जाती हैं और जून-जुलाई में बोई जाती हैं तथा अक्टूबर-नवंबर में काटी जाती हैं। इन फसलों को अधिक पानी की आवश्यकता होती है। चावल, सोयाबीन, और कपास खरीफ की प्रमुख फसलें हैं। गेहूँ एक रबी की फसल है जिसे अक्टूबर-नवंबर में बोया जाता है और मार्च-अप्रैल में काटा जाता है। यह ठंडे मौसम में उगाई जाती है और इसे कम पानी की आवश्यकता होती है। इसलिए, गेहूँ खरीफ की फसल नहीं है।

Extra Facts:
भारत में फसलों को मुख्यतः तीन ऋतुओं में बाँटा गया है: खरीफ, रबी, और जायद। खरीफ फसलों में मक्का, बाजरा, मूंगफली, और अरहर भी शामिल हैं। रबी फसलों में सरसों, चना, और जौ प्रमुख हैं। जायद फसलें गर्मियों में उगाई जाती हैं, जैसे तरबूज, खीरा, और ककड़ी। भारत की कृषि अर्थव्यवस्था में इन फसलों का महत्वपूर्ण योगदान है।

question:
In rainforests which kind of cultivation is practiced?

[SSC CGL 2022]
options: Dry farming
Vertical farming
Terrace farming
Slash and burn
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Slash and burn

Explanation:
In rainforests, 'Slash and Burn' cultivation is primarily practiced. It is also known as 'Shifting Cultivation'. This is an ancient agricultural method where forests are cut and burned to make the land suitable for farming. This technique is prevalent in tropical rainforests because the soil here loses fertility quickly. Farmers cultivate a small plot for 2-3 years and then move to a new area. This is ecologically harmful as it leads to deforestation.

Extra Facts:
Shifting Cultivation is mainly practiced in the rainforests of Northeast India, South America, Africa, and Southeast Asia. In India, it is called 'Jhum' in Assam, 'Ponam' in Kerala, 'Podu' in Andhra Pradesh, and 'Dahiya' in Odisha. This method reduces soil fertility and increases carbon emissions. Sustainable agriculture is recommended as an alternative.

वर्टिकल फार्मिंग
वेदिका कृषि

solution_hi:
हल: सही उत्तर है कर्तन एवं दहन कृषि

Explanation:
वर्षावनों में मुख्य रूप से 'कर्तन एवं दहन कृषि' (Slash and Burn) की जाती है। इसे 'झूम कृषि' भी कहते हैं। यह एक प्राचीन कृषि पद्धति है जिसमें वनों को काटकर और जलाकर भूमि को कृषि योग्य बनाया जाता है। यह विधि उष्णकटिबंधीय वर्षावनों में प्रचलित है क्योंकि यहाँ की मिट्टी उर्वरता जल्दी खो देती है। किसान एक छोटे से भूखंड पर 2-3 साल तक खेती करके फिर नए क्षेत्र में चले जाते हैं। यह पारिस्थितिकी के लिए हानिकारक है क्योंकि इससे वनों का विनाश होता है।

Extra Facts:
झूम कृषि मुख्यतः उत्तर-पूर्व भारत, दक्षिण अमेरिका, अफ्रीका और दक्षिण-पूर्व एशिया के वर्षावनों में प्रचलित है। भारत में इसे असम में 'झूम', केरल में 'पोनम', आंध्र प्रदेश में 'पोडु' और ओडिशा में 'दहिया' कहते हैं। इस पद्धति से मिट्टी की उर्वरता कम हो जाती है और कार्बन उत्सर्जन बढ़ता है। वैकल्पिक रूप से 'टिकाऊ कृषि' अपनाने की सलाह दी जाती है।

jute and cotton
jowar and maize
millet and jute

Explanation:
The Green Revolution in India was initiated in the 1960s to increase food grain production. It introduced high-yielding varieties (HYVs) of rice and wheat, which required chemical fertilizers and irrigation for optimal output. The primary goal was to ensure food security, which was successfully achieved. States like Punjab, Haryana, and Western Uttar Pradesh became the major hubs of this revolution.

Extra Facts:
Dr. M.S. Swaminathan is regarded as the 'Father of the Green Revolution' in India. While it significantly boosted food production, it also led to ecological concerns like soil degradation and groundwater depletion. The revolution also promoted farm mechanization (tractors, harvesters, etc.). Even today, rice and wheat remain India's staple crops.

question:
Shifting agriculture is known as ______ in the Western Ghats.

[SSC CPO 2023]
options: kumari
dahiya
waltre
koman
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is kumari

Explanation:
Shifting agriculture in the Western Ghats is known as 'Kumari'. This farming practice is primarily adopted by tribal communities, where forests are cleared and burned for cultivation. Once the soil fertility declines, farmers move to new areas. This traditional method impacts ecology but is part of local culture. The biodiversity and sloping terrain of the Western Ghats make it suitable for this type of agriculture.

Extra Facts:
Shifting agriculture is known by different names in various regions, such as 'Jhum' (Northeast India), 'Podu' (Andhra Pradesh and Odisha), and 'Bewar' (Central India). This practice promotes soil erosion and deforestation, leading to environmental issues. The Indian government has initiated schemes to regulate it.

question:
When did the first phase of Green Revolution started?

[SSC GD 2022]
options: Mid 1960s
Mid 1970s
Mid 1980s
Mid 1950s
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Mid 1960s

Explanation:
The first phase of the Green Revolution began in the mid-1960s. It was a significant agricultural transformation aimed at increasing food grain production through the use of high-yielding variety (HYV) seeds, chemical fertilizers, irrigation facilities, and modern farming techniques. The primary focus was on wheat and rice crops. In India, it started around 1965-66, making the country self-sufficient in food grain production. The initiative was led by Dr. M.S. Swaminathan, known as the 'Father of the Green Revolution in India'.

Extra Facts:
While the Green Revolution helped India overcome food shortages, it also had some negative impacts, such as soil fertility depletion, declining water tables, and excessive use of chemical fertilizers. Despite this, it marked a revolutionary change in agriculture, ensuring food security. The second phase began in the 1980s, incorporating more crops.

question:
Which of the following statements is correct ?
I. Maize requires moderate temperature, rainfall and lots of sunshine.
II. Jute grows well on alluvial soil and requires high temperature, heavy rainfall and humid climate.

[SSC CHSL 2022]
options: Neither I nor II
Only I
Only II
Both I and II
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Both I and II

Explanation:

 

Maize: Maize cultivation requires moderate temperature (20-27°C), moderate rainfall (50-100 cm), and plenty of sunshine. It is grown in tropical and subtropical regions.

 

Jute: Jute thrives in alluvial soil and requires high temperature (24-37°C), heavy rainfall (150-250 cm), and humid climate. It is mainly cultivated in West Bengal, Bihar, and Assam.

 


Both statements are correct as they accurately describe the ideal cultivation conditions for these crops.

Extra Facts:

 

Maize is called the 'Queen of Cereals' and is a C4 plant exhibiting high photosynthetic rates.

 

Jute is known as the 'Golden Fibre' and is a major cash crop of India. It grows well in the fertile Gangetic-Brahmaputra delta.

 

In India, West Bengal is the largest producer of jute, while Karnataka is the largest producer of maize.

question_hi:

मक्का (Maize): मक्के की खेती के लिए मध्यम तापमान (20-27°C), मध्यम वर्षा (50-100 cm) और अधिक धूप की आवश्यकता होती है। यह उष्णकटिबंधीय और उपोष्णकटिबंधीय क्षेत्रों में उगाया जाता है।

 

पटसन (Jute): पटसन को जलोढ़ मृदा की आवश्यकता होती है और यह उच्च तापमान (24-37°C), भारी वर्षा (150-250 cm) और आर्द्र जलवायु में अच्छी तरह से विकसित होता है। यह मुख्य रूप से पश्चिम बंगाल, बिहार और असम में उगाया जाता है।

question:
Which of the following is a drought-tolerant crop?

[RRB NTPC CBT]
options: Jute
Rice
Millet
Sugarcane
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Millet

Explanation:
Millet is a drought-tolerant crop that can be grown in low-rainfall regions. It thrives well in arid and semi-arid climates due to its deep root system, which allows it to withstand water scarcity. Millet is primarily cultivated in states like Rajasthan, Gujarat, Haryana, and Uttar Pradesh. It is a nutrient-rich grain, high in protein, fiber, and minerals. Other options like rice and sugarcane require substantial water, while jute is a fiber crop with low drought tolerance.

Extra Facts:
Drought-tolerant crops are those that can grow with minimal water and endure prolonged dry conditions. These include sorghum, millet, finger millet (ragi), chickpea, and groundnut. Such crops are vital for farmers in India's dry regions as they provide good yields despite climate change and erratic rainfall. Millets are termed 'nutri-cereals', and the year 2023 was declared the 'International Year of Millets' to promote their cultivation.

Explanation:
बाजरा एक सूखा सहनीय फसल है जो कम वर्षा वाले क्षेत्रों में उगाई जा सकती है। यह शुष्क और अर्ध-शुष्क जलवायु में अच्छी तरह से विकसित होता है क्योंकि इसकी जड़ें गहरी होती हैं और यह पानी की कमी को सहन कर सकता है। बाजरा मुख्य रूप से राजस्थान, गुजरात, हरियाणा और उत्तर प्रदेश जैसे राज्यों में उगाया जाता है। यह एक पोषक तत्वों से भरपूर अनाज है जिसमें प्रोटीन, फाइबर और खनिज प्रचुर मात्रा में पाए जाते हैं। अन्य विकल्प जैसे चावल और गन्ना को अधिक पानी की आवश्यकता होती है, जबकि जूट एक रेशेदार फसल है जो सूखे के प्रति कम सहनशील है।

question:
In which of the following ways were farmers encouraged to begin to use high yielding variety seeds ?

[SSC CPO 2024]
options: Farmers’ children were given free education in government colleges and universities.
Agricultural labourers were paid wages directly by the government.
Farmers were given monetary support in cash to cultivate food grains.
The government provided seeds and other inputs at prices lower than those prevailing in the market.
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is The government provided seeds and other inputs at prices lower than those prevailing in the market.

Explanation:
During the 'Green Revolution' in India, farmers were encouraged to use High Yielding Variety (HYV) seeds. The government facilitated this by providing seeds, fertilizers, pesticides, and irrigation facilities at subsidized rates lower than market prices. This policy aimed to increase agricultural productivity and ensure food security. By making these inputs economically viable for farmers, it motivated them to adopt new agricultural technologies, leading to significant growth in food grain production.

Extra Facts:
The Green Revolution made India self-sufficient in food grain production during the 1960s-70s. Its major impact was seen in Punjab, Haryana, and Western Uttar Pradesh. Dr. M.S. Swaminathan is regarded as the father of India's Green Revolution. While it dramatically increased wheat and rice productivity, it also led to environmental concerns like groundwater depletion and soil health degradation due to excessive chemical use.

question:
Which state of India has the biggest consumption of fertiliser (in kg per hectare)?

[RRB NTPC CBT]
options: Haryana
West Bengal
Andhra Pradesh
Punjab
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Punjab

Explanation:
Punjab is the state with the highest fertilizer consumption per hectare in India. This is primarily because Punjab is known as the 'Granary of India' and practices intensive farming for high yields of wheat and rice. To maintain soil fertility and achieve high productivity, chemical fertilizers are used extensively. Additionally, Punjab has excellent irrigation facilities, enabling farmers to grow multiple crops, which depletes soil nutrients and increases the need for fertilizers.

Extra Facts:

The Indian government has launched schemes like the Paramparagat Krishi Vikas Yojana (PKVY) to promote organic farming and reduce dependency on chemical fertilizers.

question:
Which of the following food grains highly benefited from the Green Revolution?

[SSC CHSL 2024]

Wheat
Barley
Millet
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Wheat

Explanation:
The Green Revolution (1960s-70s) brought a transformative change in India's agricultural production. Wheat benefited the most due to the introduction of High Yielding Varieties (HYV) and expansion of irrigation facilities, which significantly increased its yield. Wheat productivity increased more than 3-fold, making India self-sufficient in food grain production. Additionally, the use of chemical fertilizers and pesticides further boosted wheat production.

Extra Facts:
The key scientist behind the Green Revolution was Dr. M.S. Swaminathan, known as the 'Father of the Green Revolution'. This revolution turned Punjab, Haryana, and Western Uttar Pradesh into the 'Granary of India'. However, it also led to issues like groundwater depletion and soil pollution. Rice also benefited from the Green Revolution, but not as much as wheat.

It led to a significant increase in the production of wheat and rice, making India self-sufficient in food grain production. While it helped India overcome food shortages, it also led to issues like soil degradation, groundwater depletion, and excessive use of chemical fertilizers. The Green Revolution also promoted farm mechanization.

question:
Which of the following crops is the only genetically modified (GM) crop approved for commercial cultivation in India?

[SSC CHSL 2023]
options: Bt Brinjal
Mustard
Bt Cotton
Tomato
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Bt Cotton

Explanation:
Bt Cotton is the only genetically modified (GM) crop approved for commercial cultivation in India. It was permitted by the Indian government in 2002. Bt Cotton contains a gene derived from the bacterium Bacillus thuringiensis (Bt), which provides resistance against pests, particularly the bollworm. This significantly improves crop yield and reduces pesticide use. States like Maharashtra, Gujarat, and Andhra Pradesh are major producers of Bt Cotton, contributing substantially to India's cotton output.

Extra Facts:
Genetically Modified (GM) crops are plants whose DNA has been altered using genetic engineering to introduce traits like pest resistance or enhanced nutrition. Although Bt Brinjal was developed in India, it was not approved due to environmental and health concerns. Currently, GM Mustard (DMH-11) is under consideration but has not yet received clearance for commercial farming.

बीटी कपास भारत में व्यावसायिक खेती के लिए स्वीकृत एकमात्र आनुवांशिक रूप से संशोधित (GM) फसल है। इसे वर्ष 2002 में भारत सरकार द्वारा अनुमति दी गई थी। बीटी कपास में बैसिलस थुरिंजिएन्सिस (Bt) नामक बैक्टीरिया से प्राप्त जीन को शामिल किया गया है, जो कीटों के विरुद्ध प्रतिरोधक क्षमता प्रदान करता है। यह विशेष रूप से कपास की फसल को बॉलवर्म जैसे कीटों से बचाता है, जिससे उत्पादकता में वृद्धि होती है। भारत में कपास उत्पादन में बीटी कपास का महत्वपूर्ण योगदान है, विशेषकर महाराष्ट्र, गुजरात और आंध्र प्रदेश जैसे राज्यों में।

Extra Facts:
आनुवांशिक रूप से संशोधित (GM) फसलें वे फसलें हैं जिनके जीन में वैज्ञानिक तरीकों से परिवर्तन किया गया होता है ताकि उनमें विशेष गुण जैसे कीट प्रतिरोधकता, रोग प्रतिरोधकता या उच्च पोषक तत्व जोड़े जा सकें। भारत में बीटी बैंगन को भी विकसित किया गया था, लेकिन पर्यावरण और स्वास्थ्य संबंधी चिंताओं के कारण इसे व्यावसायिक खेती के लिए अनुमति नहीं दी गई। वर्तमान में, जीएम सरसों (DMH-11) पर भी विचार किया जा रहा है, लेकिन इसे अभी तक मंजूरी नहीं मिली है।

question:
Shifting Agriculture is also known as Jhum in __________.

[SSC MTS 2022]
options: Maharashtra
Assam
Rajasthan
Karnataka
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Assam

Explanation:
Shifting Agriculture is known by different names in various regions. In the northeastern states of India, particularly Assam, Mizoram, Nagaland, and Meghalaya, it is called 'Jhum'. This agricultural practice involves clearing forests by cutting and burning to create arable land. Crops are cultivated for a few years until the soil fertility declines, after which the process is repeated in a new area. This traditional method is practiced by tribal communities but is also considered harmful to the environment due to deforestation and soil degradation.

Extra Facts:
Shifting Agriculture is known by various names across India. In Andhra Pradesh, it is called 'Podu', in Kerala 'Punam', in Odisha 'Dahiya', and in Madhya Pradesh 'Bewar'. This practice is mainly prevalent in rainforests and hilly areas. However, it leads to problems like soil erosion and loss of biodiversity, prompting the government to introduce schemes to regulate it.

Explanation:
स्थानांतरित कृषि (Shifting Agriculture) को विभिन्न क्षेत्रों में अलग-अलग नामों से जाना जाता है। भारत के पूर्वोत्तर राज्यों, विशेषकर असम, मिजोरम, नागालैंड और मेघालय में इसे 'झूम' कहा जाता है। यह कृषि पद्धति वनों को काटकर और जलाकर खेती योग्य भूमि तैयार करने पर आधारित है। इसके बाद कुछ वर्षों तक खेती की जाती है और फिर भूमि की उर्वरता कम होने पर नई जगह पर इस प्रक्रिया को दोहराया जाता है। यह पारंपरिक तरीका आदिवासी समुदायों द्वारा अपनाया जाता है, लेकिन यह पर्यावरण के लिए हानिकारक भी माना जाता है।

Extra Facts:
स्थानांतरित कृषि को विभिन्न राज्यों में अलग-अलग नामों से जाना जाता है। आंध्र प्रदेश में इसे 'पोडू', केरल में 'पुनम', ओडिशा में 'दहिया' और मध्य प्रदेश में 'बेवर' कहते हैं। यह कृषि पद्धति मुख्य रूप से वर्षा वनों और पहाड़ी क्षेत्रों में प्रचलित है। हालांकि, इससे मृदा अपरदन और जैव विविधता की हानि जैसी समस्याएं उत्पन्न होती हैं, इसलिए सरकार ने इसे नियंत्रित करने के लिए कई योजनाएं शुरू की हैं।

question:
Which of the following crops takes almost a year to grow?

[SSC MTS 2024]
options: Ragi
Soyabean
Sugarcane
Groundnut
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Sugarcane

Explanation:
Sugarcane is a long-duration crop that takes approximately 10-12 months to mature fully. It is a tropical crop that requires abundant water and sunlight. Sugarcane is primarily cultivated in states like Uttar Pradesh, Maharashtra, Karnataka, Tamil Nadu, and Andhra Pradesh. This crop is a major source of sugar production and plays a significant role in India's economy. Other options like Ragi, Soyabean, and Groundnut are short-duration crops that take only a few months to mature.

Extra Facts:
Sugarcane cultivation requires a temperature of 25-32°C and an annual rainfall of 75-150 cm. It thrives best in black soil and loamy soil. India is the second-largest sugar producer in the world, contributing nearly 20% of global sugarcane production. Apart from sugar, sugarcane is also used to produce jaggery, alcohol, and biofuel. This crop can be grown in both Rabi and Kharif seasons, but most farmers cultivate it during the Kharif season.

Explanation:
गन्ना (Sugarcane) एक दीर्घकालिक फसल है जिसे पूर्ण रूप से तैयार होने में लगभग 10-12 महीने का समय लगता है। यह एक उष्णकटिबंधीय फसल है जिसे भारी मात्रा में पानी और धूप की आवश्यकता होती है। गन्ने की खेती मुख्य रूप से उत्तर प्रदेश, महाराष्ट्र, कर्नाटक, तमिलनाडु और आंध्र प्रदेश जैसे राज्यों में की जाती है। यह फसल चीनी उत्पादन का प्रमुख स्रोत है और भारत की अर्थव्यवस्था में महत्वपूर्ण योगदान देती है। अन्य विकल्प जैसे रागी, सोयाबीन और मूंगफली अल्पकालिक फसलें हैं जिन्हें तैयार होने में कुछ महीनों का ही समय लगता है।

question:
In which months is Rabi crop sown?

[SSC CHSL 2023]
options: April-May
October-December
February-March
September-October
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is October-December

Explanation:
Rabi crops in India are primarily sown between October and December. These crops are grown during the winter season and harvested from March to April. Rabi crops require less water as they depend on winter rains and irrigation. Major Rabi crops include wheat, chickpea, mustard, barley, and peas. These crops are predominantly cultivated in northern and northwestern regions of India, where winters are distinct.

Extra Facts:
Rabi crops are the second major cropping season in India, while Kharif (June-September) and Zaid (March-June) are the other two. Fertile loamy soil is ideal for Rabi cultivation. Key Rabi-producing states in India include Punjab, Haryana, Uttar Pradesh, and Madhya Pradesh. Wheat, a major Rabi crop, plays a crucial role in India’s food security.

solution_hi:

Explanation:
रबी की फसल भारत में मुख्य रूप से अक्टूबर से दिसंबर के बीच बोई जाती है। यह फसल शीत ऋतु में उगाई जाती है और मार्च से अप्रैल के बीच काटी जाती है। रबी फसलों को पानी की कम आवश्यकता होती है, क्योंकि इन्हें सर्दियों की हल्की वर्षा और सिंचाई पर निर्भर रहना पड़ता है। मुख्य रबी फसलों में गेहूं, चना, सरसों, जौ, मटर आदि शामिल हैं। ये फसलें भारत के उत्तरी और उत्तर-पश्चिमी क्षेत्रों में अधिक उगाई जाती हैं, जहाँ सर्दियों का मौसम स्पष्ट होता है।
